notes: Route: robots.txt (200, permissive for UA *; only /printable/ and */.html disallowed, GPTBot blocked) -> Sitemap: https://rg.ru/sitemaps/index.xml. The index is a sitemapindex of 8496 PER-DAY urlsets, one per calendar day since 2003, at the same URL with date_start/date_end unix timestamps that are MSK (UTC+3) midnights (first covering entry 1790283600 = 2026-09-25 00:00 MSK). Got the 33 entries spanning 2026-09-24..2026-10-26 (1-day margin each side), fetched each (all 200, ~71s total at 1 req/s via polite_fetch). Per-day urlset contains that day's articles plus a few late/early crossovers from adjacent days; every news article URL embeds its publication date in the path /YYYY/MM/DD/slug.html, and I verified on multiple samples that the path date EXACTLY equals page JSON-LD datePublished (date) and the visible date div (e.g. '10.10.2026 23:52'), delta 0 days. AVOID <lastmod>: it is edit time, not publication time (on the 10-10 file, 28 of 233 entries had lastmod 10-11..10-15 while page date stayed 10-10; dateModified also diverged). Listed date = URL path date only; URLs without a date in the path (~1-40/day, evergreen /post/ and section pages) are excluded because their lastmod is not a publish date and their pages carry no matching date. Result: 14128 unique URLs, 31/31 days, min 204 (2026-10-17); 09-30=633, 10-10=233, 10-20=584. Self-check: 4 random re-fetches all 200 with 2658-6270 chars of text and page date == listed date. Gotcha: the index HTML-encodes the separator as &, must html.unescape before matching, or the server silently ignores the params and returns today's dayset (I hit this in a probe and got 2026-10-26 content for a 10-10 query).
